verification_notes: Verified the saved final artifact over local HTTP at http://127.0.0.1:8131/public/artifacts/moving-day-box-labeler-gemini.html. It rendered nonblank with the expected textarea, Generate Labels & Summary button, Print Labels button, dashboard, manifest table, and printable label section. Generated labels from a messy five-box list, then edited room/priority/fragility values and regenerated; the table and label cards updated to 5 labels, 2 high-priority boxes, and 2 fragile boxes with no horizontal overflow at the desktop viewport. Prompt 1 verification found a real defect where comma-heavy contents like router, chargers, work laptop were truncated to router. Prompt 2 fixed the destructive comma chop: the final artifact preserved router, chargers, work laptop in the contents while still classifying the row as High and Fragile. The final artifact includes a viewport meta tag, responsive grid CSS, @media print rules, and a Print Labels control wired to window.print(); no copy/export/download controls are present to test. Direct browser viewport resizing was not exposed in the Chrome API, so narrow/mobile-ish verification was limited to responsive CSS/source inspection plus desktop no-overflow checks.
result_content: Moving-day box labeler that turns rough box notes into room/priority/fragility labels and a printable packing summary in one browser file.

steps.notes: One-shot response. Initial artifact rendered and generated labels, but verification found a real parsing defect: comma-heavy contents were truncated at the first comma, which justified prompt 2 under the 1-2 prompt override.

steps.prompt_exact: The tool works, but comma-heavy contents like "router, chargers, work laptop" get chopped to just "router" because the parser treats every comma as a field separator. Fix the parsing so contents keep comma lists unless the comma is clearly separating fields, and keep it as one HTML file.
steps.response_summary: Gemini revised the parser to avoid splitting contents at every comma, preserving comma-heavy item lists while still detecting priority and fragility flags.
